title.label: I want so badly to like this app

content.label: I'm not new to lifting, but I rely on apps like this for guidance. Earlier this year I used Fitbod consistently and built up to a solid weight. Then life happened, and I started having multiple weeks between sessions. The AI coach would say "I see you've been gone for a month," and then the first workout back would be a "max effort day" at or above my peak weight. It recognizes I've been away, and instead of a gradual reintroduction, it puts me in a position to get injured. I'm shocked the app expects me to lower the weights myself after time off. That's exactly what I'm paying it to do! Adapting to real life fluctuations is the feature that should justify the price.

I waited to write a review because I wanted to give an accurate assessment. I’ve been using Fitbod since June 2025, and I can honestly say I feel stronger and better than I did years ago. I love that the app keeps track of the weights I should be lifting, takes the guesswork out of planning my workouts, and with Coach Beta, even gives me a little pep talk about the exercise I’ve chosen.

One of my favorite features is the workout streak. It’s surprisingly motivating to watch that number grow, and I’ve now logged more than 200 workouts. I’m someone who prefers working out on my own rather than with a personal trainer, and Fitbod gives me the structure and guidance I want while still letting me do exactly that. After 16 months, I’m still using it consistently, and that probably says more than anything else. Highly recommend.

title.label: Strong app that depends on what you need

content.label: Fitbod is a strong app for a lot of people. I had been working out kind of the same for a year and a half and was getting bored and needed to change things up. Fitbod helped push me to do different exercises. I like that it allows you to add your gym, which is about 95% accurate on what weight they have. However, it does not allow you to do the same thing with the second gym if you got more than one gym. I like that has timers between sets that you can change, but it doesn’t learn if you like less time between sets. The standard is pretty long, like two minutes on a lot of exercises. If you have not done a lot of weight workouts, this will help you train you how to do them and push you to do different things. So probably a five star rating for a beginner or an intermediate person. For someone like me who’s worked out for a number of years, it still needs a little bit of development

However it is amazing and really helps me spread my horizons and stay constant. The app is super helpful and never feels like it’s going against my workout. I can easily change my work out passed on time, full body or specific muscles, or my overall goal. The app has also every workout and machine so you’ll always find either a new work out or ones you were previously doing. I suggest it to everyone I know, even if they don’t keep it, it has a great starting point. The app also allows you to send people a free trial to try it out. I would say the only problems I have with the app are usually small and are more small nitpicks than problems.

Great product with a lot of potential. One simple improvement could make Fitbod significantly better: allow users to save the sports they play or are training for in their preferences. The AI could then incorporate those sports into its existing variables when building workouts.

For example, if I select golf and surfing, Fitbod could tailor my strength, mobility, power, and recovery work around the physical demands of those sports while still considering my goals, available equipment, training history, muscle recovery, and workout duration.

It seems like a natural extension of what Fitbod already does well and would make the AI-generated workouts feel much more personalized and purposeful.
